packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-14 - unverified image-only reading

Exposure statement: No proposed identification of the work or author was in my context. The only text beyond the brief and PROMPT.md was the packet/batch path name ("stams-c5ugo-batch-6"); a modern pencil shelfmark is visible on the leaf itself (see survey). I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (Read for brief, PROMPT.md, images; Write/Edit for this file).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- Single paper or parchment strip/leaf, landscape orientation, photographed on black with colour checker and ruler; a plastic spatula/pointer lies over the lower edge centre.
- One block of text, single column, long lines running the full width; about 23 lines visible. Text appears cut at the top (first line partly trimmed) and at the right edge (line ends run off the leaf). Left edge has a margin with a few marginal marks (e.g. a mark at the far left of line 1 outside the leaf? "...tt +" and a vertical marginal note at lower left, lines ~15-20).
- Horizontal fold/crease lines across the middle (around lines 9-10 and 13-14); a tear/repair at left edge near line 9-10.
- Lower third (approx. lines 15-21) is badly abraded/faded and stained; text there is much harder.
- Script: German vernacular cursive (Bastarda/cursiva-type), brown ink, no rubrics, no enlarged initials, no running title visible. Virgulae (/) used as punctuation within lines.
- Modern pencil note bottom right: "Stams, StA, Frg. 40x" (shelfmark, not an identification of the text).
- Observed content type (tentative): continuous vernacular prose, apparently addressed to a "du" (second person) - letter- or devotional-dialogue-like. No lemma/commentary division visible.

Plan: transcribe each tile in turn, left part of lines from the left tile(s), continuation from right tile(s), plus the abraded lower block as far as possible.

TILE image-002.jpg (top-left of leaf; covers left ~half of lines 1-14 of the text block)
Conventions: "/" = virgula in MS; ' - ' = a dash-like stroke in MS; (..) expansion; ? after uncertain word.
002.00  [descenders only of a trimmed line above; unreadable]
002.01  [ver?]meyden / alle sünde / un(d) schantt[...]
002.02  [margin: "..tt +" with a cross-like mark] sünder sälikeit? amen / gott sy gena[d ...]
002.03  ü(ber)? nun? es sy der selen nitt / das [...]
002.04  verkeret? sich warlich pald / wo? [...]   ("pald" written in darker ink, possibly retraced)
002.05  Nun sych / das ist deiner schwester gesch[...]
002.06  mich darnn? nun wol gehaltn - Nun [...]
002.07  für gröslich? schon? / den ich hab dir? [...]
002.08  fänglich? hast hin? sy wellt? zyhe(n)? [...]   (first word with superscript a/o over first vowel; "anfänglich"? left edge)
002.09  das ich dir so mitt grosser marter? [...]
002.10  wol ich auch das gelt nun? hab [...]
002.11  gesehen? - So bytt nur? auch das ma[...]
002.12  den weges? selde? pelanst? / du ist? so [...]   (crease runs through this line; letters damaged)
002.13  auch mitt lediger? lassen? / sy welle dich [...]
002.14  dich weysen? er auss sin? hertzen / darum [...]
Notes: superscript small o/e/u marks over vowels (umlaut/diphthong signs) are frequent (sünder, über, gröslich, nun). Final -n often by a stroke over the preceding letter ("gehaltn", "darum"). Readings with ? are tentative.

TILE image-003.jpg (top-right of leaf; overlaps image-002 by a few words; continues lines 1-14 to the right edge)
Line numbers follow this image from the top; they correspond to the same text lines as 002.01-002.14. Overlap words are given first in [ ] where repeated.
003.00  [descenders of trimmed line above only]
003.01  [schantt] / nitt clagen? - di hochfartt ain? [... cut at right edge]
003.02  [sy genad] / das mans? erlich? un(d) schan[d?] ge[...]
003.03  [nitt] / das gelungt? das der ist di genad gott[es?]
003.04  [pald] / wye den deiner schwester geschehen ist
003.05  [schwe]ster geschehen - Warlich warlich ich mag
003.06  [gehal]tn - Nun so wayss? nun / das ich dir auch da[...]
003.07  [hab dir] so trewlich? vorgehallt / da du an
003.08  [welle] zyhe(n)? - un(d) mich auch grüslich? ver ...st? [edge]
003.09  [mart]er? / dittz? mal das zu wissen thun? / dy[...]   ("mal" in darker ink, retraced like "pald" above; a dark ink blot after it)
003.10  [hab] / ist aber das an allen dingen dy
003.11  [au]ch das mach? an dir an / das du dich mitt
003.12  [...] mitt grossem? [large looped letters, possibly a later pen trial or a retraced word: "Wyst?"] st? wellen du
003.13  [welle] dich so wol gleich? mache(n)? / so lassen? an
003.14  darum(m) wer wern? dich [rest of line cut at tile bottom]
Joined reading of lines 3-5 across both tiles (tentative):
  ü(ber)? nun es sy der selen nitt / das gelungt? das der ist di genad gott[es]
  verkeret sich warlich pald / wye den deiner schwester geschehen ist
  Nun sych / das ist deiner schwester geschehen - Warlich warlich ich mag

TILE image-004.jpg (bottom-left of leaf; top lines overlap 002.11-002.14; then the lower block to the foot of the leaf)
004.00  [top of trimmed line = 002.11, "gesehen? - So bytt..."; only lower half visible]
004.01  den weges? selde? gelangst? / du ist? so [= 002.12, overlap]
004.02  auch mitt ledig lasst / sy welle dich [= 002.13, overlap; "lasst" with two tall long-s, one ascender very large]
004.03  dich weysen? ar? auss yer? hertzen / darum(m) [= 002.14, overlap]
004.04  [ist?] nitt? auch hie yetz? wenig? un(d) ton[...]   (new line 15 of text block)
004.05  nicht? wye oft hab ich dich auch so trew[lich?]
004.06  von yeder? geselleschaft - für war fü[r war]
004.07  [rec?]hte? zu kumen? [...] durch sich? [...]   (lines 7-9 abraded and overlaid by faint offset/show-through letters in a lighter ink; a small red mark near "kumen")
004.08  [illegible: 2-3 words, abraded] kristenlich? oder? ze schlag[en?]
004.09  [illegible: 1 word] das gesehen? wol? eben? war [...]
004.10  vor allen dingen sol? gottes farcht? / forcht?
004.11  mitt su? wyrtt? - den gott hatt gesch[affen? ...]
004.12  man sol sitten? er wille haben un(d) [...]
Below 004.12: blank lower margin; no further text.
Left margin, lower part (beside lines 004.08-004.12): a short vertical note, partly in red/brown, read bottom-to-top; I cannot read it ([illegible], perhaps 3-4 characters plus a word).

TILE image-005.jpg (bottom-right of leaf; top lines overlap 003.11-003.14; continues lines 15-23 to the right edge)
005.00  [...]ch das mach? an dir an / das du dich mitt [= 003.11, overlap]
005.01  [...] mitt grossem? [large looped letters "Wyst?"] st? wellen du [= 003.12, overlap]
005.02  [w]elle dich so wol gleich? mache(n) / so lassen? a[n] [= 003.13, overlap]
005.03  [hertz]en / darum(m) wer wern? dich nitt - damitt
005.04  [...] un(d) tondt? zu spott un(d) zu schantt w[...]   (= continues 004.04)
005.05  [auch] so trewlich gepetten? / das du dich gem[...]   (= continues 004.05)
005.06  [für] war für war es wirtt gewaniger? sun[...]   (= continues 004.06; "gewaniger" very uncertain)
005.07  [durch] sich? geselschaft ver[füret?] [...] [illegible, abraded]   (= continues 004.07; offset letters overlay)
005.08  [ze] schlagen? wirtt wen es ist? geselschaf[t]   (= continues 004.08)
005.09  [eben] war sich? hiet? lasster? [illegible] sum? [...]   (= continues 004.09; abraded)
005.10  [got]tes farcht un(d) gott widersprech? [illegible] schanden?   (= continues 004.10)
005.11  [ha]tt geschaft / er hatt nitt verpotten / sun[der?]   (= continues 004.11)
005.12  [ha]ben un(d) lass dir nitt perding? nitt so ham? [...]   (= continues 004.12)
Below: modern pencil "Stams, StA, Frg. 40x" (shelfmark).

JOINED TENTATIVE READING OF THE LOWER BLOCK (text lines 14-23, left tile + right tile):
  dich weysen ar? auss yer? hertzen / darum(m) wer wern? dich nitt - damitt
  [ist?] nitt? auch hie yetz? wenig? un(d) tondt? zu spott un(d) zu schantt w[...]
  nicht? wye oft hab ich dich auch so trewlich gepetten? / das du dich gem[...]
  von yeder? geselleschaft - für war für war es wirtt gewaniger? sun[...]
  [rec?]hte? zu kumen? [...] durch sich? geselschaft ver[...] [illegible]
  [illegible] kristenlich? oder? ze schlagen? wirtt wen es ist? geselschaft
  [illegible] das gesehen? wol? eben? war sich? hiet? lasster? [illegible]
  vor allen dingen sol? gottes farcht un(d) gott widersprech? [illegible] schanden?
  mitt su? wyrtt? - den gott hatt geschaft / er hatt nitt verpotten / sun[der]
  man sol sitten? er wille haben un(d) lass dir nitt perding? nitt so ham?

SECOND FACE (verso) - image-006.jpg overview, image-007.jpg tile
(Correction to the survey: the packet does contain a second face; I had not opened it when writing the survey.)
- image-006.jpg: same leaf, other side. No main-text writing visible. Horizontal fold/crease lines and repair strips across the middle; a few small holes/stains. Faint show-through of the recto text only.
- Modern pencil note at top, written upside down relative to the photo; pencil shelfmark bottom right "Stams, StA, Frg. 40v".
- image-007.jpg (top-left tile of verso): the upside-down pencil note, read rotated 180 degrees: "[word, possibly 'Ausgebunden?' / 'aus ...' - seen only in the overview] II/6? 33 (aus J. 15[3?]5?)" - digits uncertain; looks like an archival note recording a binding/volume signature and a year. Rest of tile blank paper.

- image-008.jpg (top-right tile of verso): completes the upside-down pencil note. Rotated 180 degrees, the full note reads: "Einband zu II/G? 33 (aus J. 15[3?]5?)" - "II/G" vs "II/6" and the year digits uncertain. Archival binding note, not text of the fragment. Rest of tile blank; fold/repair strip at bottom.

- image-009.jpg (bottom-left tile of verso): blank paper; fold lines, sewing/binding holes in a vertical row near the right of the tile, stains, a red fibre at left edge. No writing.

- image-010.jpg (bottom-right tile of verso): blank paper; continuation of the vertical row of sewing holes (left of tile), a hole on the central fold, pencil shelfmark "Stams, StA, Frg. 40v". No writing.

LIMITATIONS
- Verso is blank apart from modern pencil notes. Top line trimmed (only descenders/partial letters), right-edge line ends cut on several lines (only a letter or two lost per line, judging from the right-tile margin).
- Lines 7-10 of the lower block (004.07-004.09 / 005.07-005.09) are abraded and overlaid by faint offset or show-through writing; my readings there are fragmentary.
- Many word readings are tentative (marked ?); I have not normalised spelling. Superscript vowels (umlaut/diphthong marks) are shown only where I was confident (ü, ä); others omitted.
- Areas left unread: the trimmed top line; the vertical marginal note at lower left; the abraded middles of lines 18-20.
- A wider-contrast or UV/multispectral crop of the lower third would help lines 18-20.
